title: Human Germline Gene Editing
rootClaim: Parents should be legally permitted to genetically modify human embryos for non-medical inheritable enhancements (intelligence, physical traits, longevity).

branches.text: Procreative Liberty & Human Enhancement: Individuals have a fundamental right to improve the biological trajectory of their offspring.

children.text: Procreative Beneficence: Parents have a moral obligation to give their children the best genetic start in life, reducing vulnerability to disease and cognitive limitations.
Consent Paradox: Future generations cannot consent to permanent genetic alterations that alter their identity and biology forever.
Unedited Inheritance Argument: Natural biological reproduction also passes on unchosen random genetic mutations without future child consent.
Eradication of Heritable Suffering: Germline modification permanent removes monogenic diseases (like Huntington's, cystic fibrosis) from family lineages forever.
Slippery Slope to Enhancement: The boundary between disease prevention and cognitive/cosmetic enhancement is impossible to regulate cleanly.

branches.text: Social Inequality, Eugenics, and Biological Stratification: Commercial germline editing risks creating permanent genetic caste systems.

children.text: Genetic Class Divide: Wealthy families who can afford enhancements will compound their socio-economic advantages into innate biological advantages, entrenching inequality.
Universal Public Healthcare Provision: State-funded access to genetic technologies can democratize enhancements and eliminate baseline genetic disadvantages.
Erosion of Unconditional Acceptance: Parents may come to view children as customizable consumer products, reducing parental tolerance for non-conforming traits.
Historical Analogy: Environmental interventions like private tutoring, elite schooling, and music lessons already represent heavy parental customization without destroying parental love.

definitions.description: Changes to DNA in reproductive cells (sperm, eggs, embryos) that are passed down to future generations.
The principle that parents are morally obligated to select embryos expected to have the best possible quality of life.
The division of society into distinct socioeconomic classes reinforced by genetic enhancements.
Genetic edits made to non-reproductive cells that treat a patient without being inherited by future offspring.
